```{r setup, include = FALSE}
library(MixSIARPFN)
ok <- MixSIARPFN:::networks_ready()   # the code needs the networks (see pfn_networks())
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = ok,
                      fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5, out.width = "100%")
num <- function(x, digits = 2) if (ok) format(round(x, digits), nsmall = digits) else "?"
```

This follows MixSIAR's storm petrel example script (`mixsiar_script_stormpetrel.R`),
based on Bicknell et al. (2014). It uses a mixing model for movement rather than diet:
the "mixture" is juvenile (non-breeding) birds, caught in three regions (a fixed
effect), and the "sources" are adult (breeding) birds from three colonies, in Canada,
Iceland and Scotland. The model estimates what share of the juveniles in each region
are isotopically like each colony. Discrimination is set to zero, since juveniles and
adults feeding in the same region should look the same. Two tracers (δ¹³C and δ¹⁵N),
and the source data are raw samples. Only the fitting call differs from MixSIAR's script:
`run_pfn()` in place of `write_JAGS_model()` and `run_model()`.

## The data

```{r load, eval = TRUE}
mix <- load_mix_data(
  filename = system.file("extdata", "stormpetrel_consumer.csv", package = "MixSIARPFN"),
  iso_names = c("d13C", "d15N"), factors = "Region", fac_random = FALSE,
  fac_nested = FALSE, cont_effects = NULL)
source <- load_source_data(
  filename = system.file("extdata", "stormpetrel_sources.csv", package = "MixSIARPFN"),
  source_factors = NULL, conc_dep = FALSE, data_type = "raw", mix)
discr <- load_discr_data(
  filename = system.file("extdata", "stormpetrel_discrimination.csv", package = "MixSIARPFN"),
  mix)
```

`load_source_data()` summarises the raw source samples to each source's mean, SD and
sample size, which is what MixSIARPFN's networks use:

```{r sources, eval = TRUE}
source$data
```

There are `r mix$N` birds in `r length(mix$FAC[[1]]$labels)` regions
(`r paste(mix$FAC[[1]]$labels, collapse = ", ")`).

```{r isospace, eval = TRUE, fig.height = 5}
plot_data(mix = mix, source = source, discr = discr)
```

## Fitting the model

Residual * Process error and MixSIAR's uninformative Dirichlet prior, as in MixSIAR's
script.

```{r fit}
time <- system.time(
  fit <- run_pfn(mix, source, discr, alpha.prior = 1,
                 resid_err = TRUE, process_err = TRUE)
)
fit
```

## Results

```{r output, results = "hide", fig.show = "hide"}
out <- output_pfn(fit, mix, source,
                  output_options = list(summary_save = FALSE, plot_post_save_pdf = FALSE))
```

```{r summary-table}
knitr::kable(round(summary_table(fit), 3))
```

```{r result-plots, fig.height = 4}
for (p in out$plots[grepl("^Region", names(out$plots))]) print(p)
```
